measured: bash examples/improve/test.sh prints 'passed 88, failed 0'; every check asserts on a value read back out of a receipt, a log line or an exit status, and the gate has a floor under the count as well as a zero-failure condition, so a gutted copy that counts nothing exits 1

all four entry documents validate against examples/end-to-end/schemas/entry.schema.json, payload.improve against schemas/improve.schema.json and the task specification against schemas/unit.schema.json, all with that example's own validator

the four doors carry four actors, four run ids, four correlation ids and four derived delegation depths (0, 1, 1, 2) through one task specification: one unit digest and one scorecard digest at all four

each door does something different and is measured doing it: human 5 iterations to verdict_pass, event 4 to budget_ceiling with 2 of 3 targets held, schedule 5 iterations across 5 fires with 4 parks in between, external 6 iterations of which the partner's own revision is one

every declared value is proved by a differential run: metrics[].scale (3.0 works micros_per_done first, 1.0 works attempts_per_done first), metrics[].direction (down puts a metric at its target and it is never worked), loop.iteration_ceiling (8 gives verdict_pass 3/3, 2 gives iteration_ceiling 1/3 with a typed escalation), budget.ceiling_micros (3000000 runs to 5 iterations, 1000000 stops at 4, 500000 is refused before a case is replayed), candidates[].value_if_promoted, candidates[].gate.unit_version, candidates[].gate.case_filter, candidates[].template, loop.per_iteration_micros (halved: the plan floor, every record's spend_micros, the learned micros and the closing cost_micros all halve over the same five iterations), promotion.rollback_to, payload.improve.fire_mode, payload.improve.boundary.ref and payload.improve.revision_offered

the gate decides: at 1.4.1-rc the first candidate fails, is declined and the checkpoint does not move; the same candidate at 1.4.0 passes, is promoted and the checkpoint advances; the pass takes 5 iterations against 4
the deliberate breakage (--promote-regardless) leaves the gate saying failed and promotes anyway, and the check that catches it names the iteration, the decision and the checkpoint that moved

an inconclusive gate is not a softer failed: the partner's revision executes 0 cases, reports inconclusive, is declined with reason gate_inconclusive and leaves the checkpoint in place, and the metric is worked again by the next candidate

the loop driver swap is by declaration and the two are compared record for record: one-iteration-per-fire writes 4 pass-parked records across 5 processes and in-one-process writes none, and the five iteration records are byte-identical between them; the drivers differ on all three declared axes

the evaluation adapter swap is by configuration (--gate/GATE=): both adapters give the same five iteration records, the same learned record and the same closing record - outcome, terminated_by, iterations, targets held, cost and final checkpoint - while differing on execution_model, trajectory_source and emit_evaluation_result

one boundary is one pass: the same boundary.ref resumes its loop at the next iteration index and opens no second loop, a different ref opens a loop that starts at index 0, and re-firing a closed pass prints REPLAY and appends zero records. Two receipts of one basename in different directories are two passes, each opening its own loop at index 0, because the driver's store is keyed on the receipt's resolved path; and a fire that finds a standing checkpoint with no loop-opened in its receipt is refused 422 at resume and records the refusal, rather than raising

eight refused documents over three registered types, each with its type and status asserted: six 422 document-invalid (a malformed envelope, a caller-declared decision rule, a revision offered at a boundary that may not offer one, a partner finding that names no revision, a specification naming another promotion authority, a specification with no iteration ceiling), one 402 budget-exhausted at the plan, one 422 criterion-unresolvable when a metric runs out of candidates

what a refusal did not write: a refused envelope leaves no receipt at all, a plan refusal leaves pass-submitted and refusal and no loop, and a refusal after work leaves refusal, learned and pass-failed in that order

no unregistered problem type is minted: six suffixes render as five registered types, and iteration-ceiling-reached comes back as the registered deadline-exceeded carrying the proposed suffix in its detail

the README's list of eleven record kinds is set-equal to the kinds the receipts hold, in both directions, and the number it spells is read back out of that set; every record of every run carries run id, correlation id, actor, derived delegation depth, entry kind, idempotency key and the boundary, plus the chain fields; the chain verifies and a one-word edit is located at the record that moved
correlation.depth is carried and not consumed: the external door with depth 1 and with depth 99 writes byte-identical records, every one at the derived depth 2

every number in the learned table is recomputed from the iteration-recorded rows at all four doors - attempts, the candidate and template that held, the distance closed, and the micros as the sum of the spend_micros those rows each carry rather than a row count times the declared price - the closing cost_micros is checked against that same sum, and the printed totals are those numbers rather than a second count

provenance.cites equals the ids the rows carry over README.md, run.py, harnesses.py, test.sh, units/, schemas/ and entries/, checked in both directions; every REF- id resolves to a file on disk; the gap table is keyed G1..G11

every quoted string in the README that sits on a line naming a record is grepped back verbatim out of one of those records (39 on this run, with the check refusing fewer than 30, whitespace-normalised), and a REF- id with an anchor on a source file is narrowed to the definition the anchor names - so a quote attributed to a neighbouring class of the same module is refused

the nine printed commands other than test.sh itself are executed as printed from the repository root and their last lines diffed against what the README promises; each step's label is held to the verb of its own promised last line, so a label saying the pass closes over a parked: line is refused; and every flag the README names exists in the runner's argument parser

the runner calls the five published interface operations and no sixth, and the capability's own design assertions hold: no in-place edit operation, a candidate that cannot carry a criterion, an iteration ceiling that cannot be omitted

the fields that name what is being improved are carried and not consumed, measured rather than asserted: a specification renamed to totally-different-id / template:something-else with a different note writes ten records against ten and moves exactly three strings of one record (unit_id, template, unit_digest), and loop.loop_ref reaches no code, no schema and no record while its neighbour loop.on_cap is refused 422 by the capability at open_loop and by this example's schema before that

the plan's 402 is a first-fire gate and a resumed fire's declared ceiling reaches nothing: 500000 refuses a first fire before a case is replayed, and the same 500000 declared on the fires that resume an open loop closes the pass at verdict_pass printing 'spent 1250000 of 500000 micros' with no refusal record (README gap G11)

no product name appears in any file of the example or in any artifact these runs wrote: 37 names, word-anchored, case-insensitive, over every file the run has written by that point, and the check prints how many it scanned
no endpoint, credential or live adapter is reachable from the directory: the loader offers dryrun and second only

each claim was closed by falsifying it, not by reading it: eight probes were applied one at a time to a copy of the example and the named check - not the suite - went red. Hardcoding the loop bound reddened only the iteration_ceiling row; hardcoding the driver reddened the fire_mode row (and four neighbours that read the schedule door's receipt); deriving the loop id without the boundary reddened the boundary row and the printed-command diffs; writing the learned record from the runner's own numbers reddened the three learned rows; drifting one word of one quote reddened the quote row; dropping one id from cites reddened the cites row; naming a product in the README reddened the product row; dropping the offered revision reddened the four rows about it; ignoring promotion.rollback_to reddened the rollback row; ignoring promotion.authority reddened the breakage row. A gutted test.sh printing 'passed 0, failed 0' exits 1 at the floor gate

claimed: that the candidates are revisions to the named templates they carry. They are labels: the gate replays the evaluation harness's registered corpus of six release-review cases at two pinned versions of its own fixture unit, and no template is read, changed or re-run. README gap G1

that the scorecard's metric names and starting values measure this repository. They are fixture values named after what this area's row asks for - tokens per done, attempts, which template held - chosen so one pass meets a failed, an inconclusive and four passing gates. What is measured is what the pass then did with them, read back out of the receipt

that a promotion promotes anything outside the loop: no baseline is promoted, no target file is written and no registry is touched, which the capability's own provenance records as its open gap. README gaps G2 and G3

that the rollback state is a rollback: every iteration record names the checkpoint a rollback would restore and nothing restores it, because the capability publishes no restore operation. README gap G4
that the held-in and held-out split the record asks for exists here: every candidate is gated over the same six cases and the only thing held out is this area's own deciding check. README gap G5

that a re-delivered iteration inside a loop returns the identical record. The capability dedupes on an iteration key (run_iteration keeps a key set) and nothing in this example re-delivers one: what is measured here is the envelope-level REPLAY on a closed pass

that any record carries a published lifecycle state. The eleven kinds are the lifecycle this example writes; working and input-required appear in no receipt, and this area's own row does not ask for the published five
that the standards named hold at the versions given; no specification page was fetched (STATUS row 14)
that the hidden deciding check for this example exists: the index looks for docs/night/hidden/improve.sh, which this author's brief did not permit writing. README gap G10
